prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed basic subjects in Mathematics and Physics.
Prior knowledge in Algebra, Calculus, Physics I, Physics II, Chemical Fundamentals of Engineering, Mechanics I, and Thermodynamics is required.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transfer, including basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students are able to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences typically demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (normally within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge of heat transfer by steady-state conduction, with or without internal heat generation, for plane, cylindrical and spherical geometries and for extended surfaces.
Knowledge of heat transfer by unsteady-state conduction, for plane, cylindrical and spherical geometries.
Ability to apply empirical correlations to calculate the film coefficient in free and forced convection in laminar and turbulent regimes for different geometries and relative fluid movements.
Ability to apply empirical correlations to calculate the film coefficient in heat transfer during phase changes (condensation and boiling) for different geometries and regimes.
Ability to apply heat transfer by radiation for heat transfer between black or gray surfaces.

Knowledge of different types of heat exchangers and ability to calculate and design convective surface heat exchangers using the logarithmic mean temperature difference (LMTD method) or the number of transfer units (NTU method).

syllabus_topics: Thermodynamics of power cycles and refrigeration machines.
5.- Forced convection in laminar and turbulent flow
teaching_methods: Comprehensive and detailed reading of chapters (self-study)
Elaboration of conceptual and synoptic schemes
Problem solving (from textbooks and virtual course)
Consulting a tutor or the teaching team (in person, by phone, or through virtual course forums)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 90% from the final exam, 5% from laboratory practicals, and 5% from continuous assessment tests (2% from PEC1 and 3% from PEC2). A minimum score of 5.5 in the exam is required to pass without continuous assessment. Laboratory practicals are compulsory, contribute 0.5 points to the final grade, and can be carried over to subsequent years. Continuous assessment tests contribute 0.5 points, are considered for the September extraordinary exam, but are not carried over to other academic years.
